title: 🛞Unlocking Your  Potential with Archetypes: Interview with Dr. Laurence Hillman

sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel, and this is the Taproot Therapy PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是乔尔，欢迎收听 Taproot 疗愈播客。

sentences.en: We've got a great interview today with Dr. Lawrence Hellman.
sentences.zh: 今天我们邀请到了劳伦斯·赫尔曼博士进行精彩的访谈。

sentences.en: He's an astrologer and an archetypal researcher who does a lot of work with businesses for coaching and consulting
sentences.zh: 他是一位占星师兼原型研究员，在商业教练和咨询领域做了大量工作，

sentences.en: and helping people get to know the different parts of their psyche that lets them be able to create and express themselves fully professionally and personally.
sentences.zh: 帮助人们了解自己心灵的不同部分，从而让他们能够在职业和个人生活中充分创造和表达自我。

sentences.en: So that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: We're going to roll that in just a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会播出这段访谈。

sentences.en: A couple things coming up with the show.
sentences.zh: 节目有一些新的动态要宣布。

sentences.en: I mean, one, these episodes are probably going to get a lot less regular, or maybe not.
sentences.zh: 我是说，第一，这些节目可能不会那么规律了，也许吧。

sentences.en: We would really like to have an in-person studio in Birmingham and prioritize in-person episodes soon.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很想在伯明翰建立一个实地录音室，并尽快将实地录制节目列为优先事项。

sentences.en: The money's not there to do that edition just yet, but hopefully by the end of next year.
sentences.zh: 目前资金还不足以支持这一点，但希望能在明年年底前实现。

sentences.en: And then also, now that Alice is getting started, hopefully her and then one of our new therapists, James Waits, can be on the show more often as time allows.
sentences.zh: 还有，既然爱丽丝已经开始了，希望她以及我们的新治疗师之一詹姆斯·韦茨，能在时间允许的情况下更频繁地出现在节目中。

sentences.en: But this is kind of one of three things pulling me in a couple directions, and I'm trying to decide how much time I can devote to it.
sentences.zh: 但这可以说是把我拉向不同方向的三件事之一，我正在努力决定能为它投入多少时间。

sentences.en: We also have kind of a new technique at Taproot, a new brain-based medicine thing that's exciting and not really ready to be unveiled completely yet.
sentences.zh: 我们在 Taproot 也有了一种新疗法，一种令人兴奋的、以大脑为基础的新医学事物，目前还没有完全准备好公开。

sentences.en: But that is going to take a certain amount of work to develop.
sentences.zh: 但这需要一定的工作量来开发。

sentences.en: If you are a listener to the show and you like it and you want to see more of a certain kind of episode or you want to see more of a certain kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 如果你是本节目的听众，你喜欢它，并且希望看到更多某种类型的节目，或者希望看到更多某种类型的内容，

sentences.en: now would be the time to reach out because I'm going to be doing my six months to seven months out planning for guests and essays that I want to write and do.
sentences.zh: 现在就是联系我的时候了，因为我接下来要开始规划未来六到七个月的嘉宾以及我想写和做的文章。

sentences.en: And it may take a little bit of a break, but if you want to send me an email, that's on our website, gettherapybirmingham.com.
sentences.zh: 节目可能会休息一小段时间，但如果你想给我发电子邮件，可以在我们的网站 gettherapybirmingham.com 上找到。

sentences.en: Joel Blackstock at gettherapybirmingham.com, but you can also see that on my bio page.
sentences.zh: 邮箱是 Joel Blackstock at gettherapybirmingham.com，不过你也可以在我的个人简介页面上看到。

sentences.en: To give me feedback for the show, that'd be great.
sentences.zh: 能为节目给我提供反馈那就太好了。

sentences.en: I know that there are some people who listen to it and a couple of you have reached out already who like it.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人一直在听，而且你们当中已经有几个人联系过我，表达了你们的喜爱。

sentences.en: And now would be the time to do that because that's what I'm going to be working on over the next month.
sentences.zh: 现在就是做这件事的时候了，因为这就是我接下来一个月要着手做的事情。

sentences.en: So I'm going to go ahead and roll that interview.
sentences.zh: 所以我这就播出那段访谈。

sentences.en: Again, this is Dr. Lawrence Selman.
sentences.zh: 再次介绍一下，这是劳伦斯·塞尔曼博士。

sentences.en: And I encourage you to check out the show notes and look at his website and some of his other work because a lot of it is interesting.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励大家查看节目shownotes，浏览他的网站以及他的其他一些作品，因为其中很多都非常有趣。

sentences.en: And thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'm here with Dr. Lawrence Selman, and he's done so much work more than I'm probably going to be able to get to.
sentences.zh: 我和劳伦斯·塞尔曼博士在这里，他做了大量的工作，超出了我可能谈及的范畴。

sentences.en: We'll try and I have a lot of questions, but I kind of like to have more of a conversation and just see where things go to.
sentences.zh: 我们会尽力而为，我有很多问题，但我更喜欢像对话一样，看看事情会聊到哪里。

sentences.en: And something about the spontaneity seems to be a little bit more authentic and go a little bit deeper.
sentences.zh: 这种随性似乎显得更加真实，也能探讨得更深一些。

sentences.en: So I don't want to introduce you too much.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想对你做太多介绍。

sentences.en: But one of my favorite things about your work is that whenever I've come across it, a lot of people who say archetypal or talking about archetypal stuff,
sentences.zh: 但关于你的作品，我最喜欢的一点是，每当我接触到它时——许多谈论原型或探讨原型相关内容的人，

sentences.en: because I was familiar with your dad's work with archetypal psychology, too, and a lot of the stuff that's come out of Pacifica in the past couple of years.
sentences.zh: 因为我也熟悉你父亲在原型心理学方面的工作，以及过去几年从太平洋萨基大学涌现出的许多成果。

sentences.en: And but a lot of the stuff gets kind of watered down when you when you encounter it to where people are really kind of talking about a cultural layer or their political bias or their you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，当你接触到很多这类内容时，它们往往会被水化或淡化，人们实际上只是在谈论文化层面、他们的政治偏见，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: you can just kind of see that what they're talking about is not really an archetypal energy or really deep, timeless thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出他们讨论的其实并非原型能量，也不是真正深层的、永恒的东西。

sentences.en: And you sort of sift through the culture to find the stuff that is really perennial, really deep.
sentences.zh: 而你却能从文化中大浪淘沙，找到那些真正具有长青意义、真正深邃的东西。

sentences.en: You know, a samurai and a knight look very different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，武士和骑士看起来非常不同。

sentences.en: But what is the thing that is similar in these in these energies in a way that's very honest and effective?
sentences.zh: 但以一种非常诚实和有效的方式来看，这些能量中相似的东西是什么？

sentences.en: And I don't I don't see a ton of that.
sentences.zh: 而我并没有看到太多这样的内容。

sentences.en: So I don't know if you agree with that or if that's that's that I'll leave it there and then hand it over to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道你是否同意这一点，或者我就把话撂这儿，然后把话语权交给你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me, Joel.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我，乔尔。

sentences.en: And I do, of course, appreciate that's a compliment.
sentences.zh: 我当然很感激，这真是一个赞美。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I'm very practical.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得我非常务实。

sentences.en: I'm a hands on kind of a person and I do coaching and leadership development and this kind of work that needs for me to be really practical.
sentences.zh: 我是一个注重实践的人，我做教练和领导力发展，这种工作需要我极其务实。

sentences.en: Things that people can do to better their lives or to, you know, make more sense of the things that don't make sense to them.
sentences.zh: 这些是可以让人类生活变得更好，或者你知道的，让那些让他们感到困惑的事情变得顺理成章的方法。

sentences.en: And archetypes are just a really good tool.
sentences.zh: 而原型正是一个非常好的工具。

sentences.en: It's a it's a way of seeing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种观察的方式。

sentences.en: I think of archetypes as wearing a certain set of glasses.
sentences.zh: 我认为原型就像是戴上了一副特定的眼镜。

sentences.en: Maybe you remember in the movie National Treasure where Nick Cage is stealing the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 也许你还记得电影《国家宝藏》中尼古拉斯·凯奇偷《独立宣言》的桥段。

sentences.en: And he is needs to find these glasses that Ben Franklin hid somewhere in a chimney, I think, with behind a brick.
sentences.zh: 他需要找到本·富兰克林藏在某个烟囱里、我想是在一块砖后面的眼镜。

sentences.en: And so he these glasses of three lenses on each eye.
sentences.zh: 于是他拿到了这副每只眼睛上有三个镜片的眼镜。

sentences.en: And then when he flips them back and forth in a certain way and gets the right combination, then suddenly on the back of the Declaration of Independence, he sees this map.
sentences.zh: 当他以某种方式前后翻转它们并得到正确的组合时，突然间，《独立宣言》的背面就显现出了这张地图。

sentences.en: To me, archetypes are very similar.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，原型非常相似。

sentences.en: They're always there.
sentences.zh: 它们一直都在。

sentences.en: They're always visible.
sentences.zh: 它们始终清晰可见。

sentences.en: But you can only see them if you if you put on a certain set of lenses.
sentences.zh: 但你只有戴上特定的眼镜才能看到它们。

sentences.en: They're not literal lenses like that.
sentences.zh: 它们不是字面意义上的那种眼镜。

sentences.en: It's a way of seeing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种观察的方式。

sentences.en: And that's something you can learn.
sentences.zh: 这是你可以学会的。

sentences.en: And once you learn that, life becomes pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 一旦你学会了，生活就会变得相当有趣。

sentences.en: So, for instance, the chocolate mousse isn't just a chocolate mousse,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，巧克力慕斯不仅仅是一道巧克力慕斯，

sentences.en: but is also then filled with the archetype of the lover or Venus or beauty or or seduction or chocolate or all those things that belong in that same archetype.
sentences.zh: 它同时还充盈着恋人、维纳斯、美、诱惑、巧克力或属于同一原型的所有这些事物的原型。

sentences.en: Like you said, like you said, it's not just the samurai and the knight, but the warrior shows up in every person in some way, shape or form can be your drive, your passion,
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，就像你说的，不仅仅是武士和骑士，战士会以某种方式、某种形状或形式出现在每个人身上，它可以是你的驱动力、你的激情，

sentences.en: your sort of instinctual targeting, your force, your ability to defend yourself, all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你那种本能的目标锁定、你的力量、你保护自己的能力，所有这些类型的东西。

sentences.en: So we have to look much bigger than limiting an archetype to something that is, you know, a literalism, like it's my anger or it's my inner warrior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须放宽视野，而不能把原型局限于某种字面化的东西，比如“这是我的愤怒”或“这是我内心的战士”。

sentences.en: That's much too small, even though we have to, of course, give them names.
sentences.zh: 那样的格局太小了，尽管我们当然必须给它们起名字。

sentences.en: And so we do call that part that you just mentioned the warrior, but it's not limited to warrior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实把刚才提到的那个部分叫做战士，但它并不局限于战士。

sentences.en: Warrior is a very wide concept.
sentences.zh: 战士是一个非常广阔的概念。

sentences.en: And so there's always the limitation of language.
sentences.zh: 因此，语言总是有局限性的。

sentences.en: So imagination plays a lot and the idea is that the words trigger something in the imagination.
sentences.zh: 所以想象力起到了很大的作用，其核心理念是这些词汇能够触发想象力中的某些东西。

sentences.en: And when you're talking about, there's archetypes at work.
sentences.zh: 当你在谈论时，有原型在起作用。

sentences.en: Is that one that you use the most?
sentences.zh: 这是你用得最多的一个吗？

sentences.en: You've got a couple of different systems and publications.
sentences.zh: 你接触过几种不同的体系和出版物。

sentences.en: Well, I'm an astrologer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是一名占星师。

sentences.en: I've been an astrologer for 47 years.
sentences.zh: 我当占星师已经 47 年了。

sentences.en: That's how I see the world.
sentences.zh: 这就是我看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: I'm an archetypal astrology, which means that I see the archetypes that are also represented in the planets as sort of the formula through which I understand the world.
sentences.zh: 我是一名原型占星师，这意味着我将那些同样体现在行星中的原型，视作我理解世界的公式。

sentences.en: Think of the 12 notes of a keyboard, five black and seven white, that make up an octave.
sentences.zh: 想象一下琴键上的 12 个音符，五个黑键和七个白键，它们共同构成了一个八度音阶。

sentences.en: And with those, you can play pretty much any song.
sentences.zh: 利用这些，你几乎可以弹奏任何歌曲。

sentences.en: And so this is the same idea that the planetary archetypes, those 10 that we tend to use as astrologers, are sort of the basis,
sentences.zh: 所以这也是同样的道理，行星原型——我们作为占星师倾向于使用的那 10 个——基本上就是基础，

sentences.en: the 10 digits with which you can grasp any situation, describe any person, anything, any piece of art, anything you want.
sentences.zh: 就像 10 个数字一样，你可以用它们来把握任何情况、描述任何人、任何事物、任何艺术品、任何你想要的东西。

sentences.en: It's an archetypal way of seeing those are the lenses, if you want, or combinations of them.
sentences.zh: 这是一种原型的观察方式，如果你愿意的话，这些就是镜片，或者是它们的组合。

sentences.en: And so that's what I use.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我所使用的。

sentences.en: Now, we started to, my partner and I, in 2016, started to work with organizations with this work.
sentences.zh: 现在，我和我的合伙人在 2016 年开始将这项工作应用于各类组织。

sentences.en: And so we translated the astrological language into an archetypal language that is more universal and doesn't bump up against some of the pushback against astrology because it has a name.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将占星术的语言转化为了一种更为普遍的原型语言，由于它有了这样的名称，它不会招致针对占星术的那些抵触情绪。

sentences.en: It's a way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思维方式。

sentences.en: It's not, it's, it's, it's not, you know, astrology that's in the back of a magazine that tells you your sun sign.
sentences.zh: 它不是，它不是那种杂志封底告诉你星座运势的占星术。

sentences.en: It's definitely not sun sign astrology.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是星座占星术。

sentences.en: What I do, a professional astrologer doesn't do sun sign astrology that will be like saying, you know, I'm, I'm six foot tall and that defines me.
sentences.zh: 我所做的，一个专业的占星师是不会去做星座占星术的，那就好比说，你知道的，“我身高六英尺，这就定义了我”。

sentences.en: There's so much more that defines me than, than my height.
sentences.zh: 定义我的东西远比我的身高要多得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, besides the sun sign, you have a moon sign, you have a Mars sign, a Venus sign, etc.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，除了太阳星座，你还有月亮星座、火星星座、金星星座等等。

sentences.en: So, so the archetypes at work model is essentially the same model as the astrological model.
sentences.zh: 所以，工作中的原型模型本质上与占星模型是同一个模型。

sentences.en: It's one way of seeing the world, which is archetypal, but we use slightly different language and we, we focus it in its expression to business and to leadership development.
sentences.zh: 这是看待世界的一种方式，也就是原型视角，但我们使用的是略有不同的语言，并且将其表达的重点放在了商业和领导力发展上。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, and I, you know, your stuff, you're, you're working with businesses, you know, I'm a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 还有，我知道你的东西，你在与企业合作，而我是一名治疗师。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I've been really loud about for a long time is how much the reliance on pure empiricism, things that we can reduce totally down to, you know,
sentences.zh: 长期以来，我一直大声疾呼的一点是，人们对纯粹经验主义的依赖有多么严重，那些我们可以完全还原的东西，你知道的，

sentences.en: something that is Cartesian and measurable in a number, which I just don't believe the psyche.
sentences.zh: 某种笛卡尔式的、可以用数字测量的事物，而我根本不相信心灵可以这样被简化。

sentences.en: I don't believe trauma.
sentences.zh: 我不相信创伤可以。

sentences.en: I don't believe the soul really can be reduced to a number.
sentences.zh: 我不相信灵魂真的可以被简化为一个数字。

sentences.en: I love science.
sentences.zh: 我热爱科学。

sentences.en: I, I, I, you know, do research and different things.
sentences.zh: 我，我，我，你知道的，也会做研究和各种事情。

sentences.en: But I've kind of moved into the things that are more conventional wisdom and there's something, you know, of, you're saying it's a lens,
sentences.zh: 但我逐渐转向了那些更符合传统智慧的事物，正如你所说，它是一个镜片，

sentences.en: like it's a mechanism of sorting this energy so that we can understand it and work with it.
sentences.zh: 就像是一种对这种能量进行分类的机制，这样我们才能理解它并运用它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which that seems to me so inevitable in therapy, whether it's the MBTI, whether it's, you know, kind of, you know, Freudian or depth, you know, wisdom of, we learned that,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这在疗愈中是如此不可避免，无论是 MBTI，还是弗洛伊德或深度心理学的智慧，我们了解到，

sentences.en: you know, you're lovable from the parent of the opposite sex, you know, but how to be in the world from the parent of the same sex.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你从异性父母那里获得被爱的感觉，但从同性父母那里学习如何在世间为人处世。

sentences.en: I mean, therapy has been doing that forever in ways that are not a hundred percent right or not measurable or not testable,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，治疗一直以来都在这样做，虽然方式并非百分之百正确，也无法衡量或测试，

sentences.en: but they're still effective in helping us tease apart who we are and understand us.
sentences.zh: 但它们在帮助我们剖析自我和理解自我方面依然有效。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure you've had some pushback from people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确信你也遭到过一些人的抵触。

sentences.en: I mean, I, a ton of the stuff I get, if I say that I like Jung or that I'm using kind of a, a somatic archetypal thing to connect people to something, I have people say, well,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我得到的很多反馈是，如果我说我喜欢荣格，或者我正在使用某种躯体原型的方法来将人们与某些事物连接起来，就会有人说，“哦，

sentences.en: you must believe all this stuff that I don't believe, you know?
sentences.zh: 那你一定相信所有这些我根本不信的东西，对吧？”

sentences.en: And it's like, I didn't say that.
sentences.zh: 而这就好比，我根本没这么说过。

sentences.en: All I said was that I was using somatic work or something.
sentences.zh: 我只是说我在使用躯体疗法或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: How do you, how do you make sense of that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待和理解这一点的？

sentences.en: We all, we all, this is great what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人，我们所有人——你说的太棒了。

sentences.en: I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: So look, we all believe a certain way and see the world in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们都有着特定的信念，并以特定的方式看待世界。

sentences.en: What's my father used to say, it doesn't matter what you believe, just be aware what tree you're sitting in when you're believing.
sentences.zh: 我父亲过去常说，你相信什么并不重要，重要的是当你在信仰时，要清楚自己正坐在哪棵树上。

sentences.en: And I think that's a lovely metaphor because, you know, as long as we're aware that when we say, I don't believe in what I can't measure,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个极好的隐喻，因为，你知道的，只要我们意识到，当我们说“我不相信无法测量的事物”时，

sentences.en: that we are operating from a left brain perspective, this idea that it has to be rational and measurable to be real.
sentences.zh: 我们其实是在从左脑的视角运作，这种观点认为事物必须是理性的、可测量的才是真实的。

sentences.en: That's a perspective.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种视角。

sentences.en: That's a certain tree to sit in.
sentences.zh: 那只是坐在一棵特定的树上。

sentences.en: It's not wrong, but it's not the only way to see.
sentences.zh: 它并没有错，但它并不是唯一的观察方式。

sentences.en: And it's just as valid as another way to see.
sentences.zh: 它与其他观察方式同样有效。

sentences.en: It's just that since the enlightenment, that way of seeing has trumped and has made everything the right way to see.
sentences.zh: 只不过自启蒙运动以来，这种观察方式占据了统治地位，把一切都变成了唯一正确的观察方式。

sentences.en: And everything else is woo-woo or weird or different.
sentences.zh: 而其他一切都被视为迷信、怪异或异端。

sentences.en: But here's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 但现在情况正在发生变化。

sentences.en: This is what's interesting, what's happening in the world right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是有趣的地方，也是目前世界上正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So we have a absolute dominance of left brain capacity, and that's what everybody needs to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们拥有绝对占据主导地位的左脑能力，这也是每个人都必须具备的。

sentences.en: That's how you get along.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何安身立命。

sentences.en: That's how you do business.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何开展业务。

sentences.en: That's how you win.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何赢得胜利。

sentences.en: That's how you, you know, data-driven, evidence-based, more data is better, you know, measure everything.
sentences.zh: 这就是你，你知道的，数据驱动、循证为本、多多益善的数据，你知道的，测量一切。

sentences.en: And if you just get enough facts, you can make the right decision.
sentences.zh: 只要你掌握足够多的事实，你就能做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: That works in a complicated world.
sentences.zh: 这在一个复杂（complicated）的世界里是行得通的。

sentences.en: And complicated, my definition of complicated is a car, for instance, is complicated.
sentences.zh: 对于复杂，我给出的定义是，比如说一辆汽车就很复杂。

sentences.en: It has a bunch of simple systems, like the windshield wiper system has, you know, a couple of wipers and a button and some, you know, a little reservoir and some hoses.
sentences.zh: 它由一堆简单的系统组成，比如雨刮器系统有，你知道的，几个雨刮器、一个按钮、一个小储水箱和一些软管。

sentences.en: And there you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And a pump.
sentences.zh: 还有一个泵。

sentences.en: If something breaks in that simple system, you can just replace the part and it works again.
sentences.zh: 如果那个简单系统中的某个部件坏了，你只需更换零件，它就能再次运转。

sentences.en: And so all of those together makes a complicated car.
sentences.zh: 所有这些组合在一起，就构成了一辆复杂的汽车。

sentences.en: And leadership in a complicated world works being data-driven to some extent.
sentences.zh: 在这样一个复杂的（complicated）世界里，领导力在某种程度上依靠数据驱动是行得通的。

sentences.en: That's what's worked pretty well for the last, you know, several hundred years since the industrialization and so on.
sentences.zh: 这就是自工业化以来过去几百年里运作得相当不错的方式。

sentences.en: However, today we're no longer in a complicated world.
sentences.zh: 然而，今天我们所处的已不再是一个复杂（complicated）的世界。

sentences.en: We live in a complex world.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个错综复杂（complex）的世界里。

sentences.en: And the difference is emergence.
sentences.zh: 两者的区别在于涌现性。

sentences.en: Things happen overnight that change everybody's playing field.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间发生的事情改变了所有人的游戏规则。

sentences.en: For instance, COVID or the wars, because we're so global and everything is so connected, supply chains, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 例如，新冠疫情或战争，因为我们如此全球化，一切都紧密相连，供应链等等，等等。

sentences.en: Everything interacts with everything else.
sentences.zh: 万物与万物相互交织。

sentences.en: It is a different playing field.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全不同的竞技场。

sentences.en: And complexity is that capability, what we call complexity capability, to deal with the things that are not linear and that aren't predictable in that sense,
sentences.zh: 而复杂性正是那种能力，我们称之为复杂性应对能力，用来处理那些非线性且无法以这种方式预测的事物，

sentences.en: that if this happens and that's going to happen, or these are the seven possibilities, we're going to pick one and so forth.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，而那也会发生，或者这有七种可能性，我们要选一种，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So complexity capability, and this is the cool thing, is a right brain capability.
sentences.zh: 所以复杂性能力——这就是最酷的地方——是一种右脑能力。

sentences.en: That belongs into the realm of those things that aren't measurable.
sentences.zh: 这属于那些无法被量化的事物的领域。

sentences.en: Imagination, creativity, dreaming, you know, sitting still and waiting for something to pop into your mind, you know, listening, reflecting, those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 想象力、创造力、做白日梦，你知道的，静静坐着等待灵光一闪，你知道的，倾听、反思，诸如此类。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Those are right brain capabilities.
sentences.zh: 这些都是右脑能力。

sentences.en: And I know this is not literal.
sentences.zh: 我知道这并非字面意思。

sentences.en: It's not that the left brain does one thing and the right brain does one thing.
sentences.zh: 并不是说左脑只做一件事，右脑也只做一件事。

sentences.en: But this way of thinking is very commonly understood what a left brain and a right brain capability is.
sentences.zh: 但这种思维方式被人们普遍用来理解什么是左脑能力和右脑能力。

sentences.en: So the unmeasurable world is actually suddenly incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个无法量化的世界突然变得极其重要。

sentences.en: The second thing has happened that about 18 months ago, AI popped up on the scene and leaders are now suddenly dealing with AI.
sentences.zh: 第二件发生的事是，大约18个月前，人工智能横空出世，领导者们现在突然需要应对AI了。

sentences.en: AI can do left brain a gazillion times faster than any leader in the world.
sentences.zh: AI处理左脑任务的速度比世界上任何领导者都要快上无数倍。

sentences.en: And therefore, a lot of the left brain skills, like being able to take massive amounts of data and analyze it and then come up with a solution out of that,
sentences.zh: 因此，许多左脑技能——比如处理海量数据并进行分析，然后从中得出解决方案——

sentences.en: can be done way faster by a computer now.
sentences.zh: 现在计算机可以做得快得多。

sentences.en: And so that's another reason why leaders need to activate their right brain.
sentences.zh: 这也是领导者需要激活右脑的另一个原因。

sentences.en: In other words, if you look at Harvard Business Review and what are people talking about in leadership, everyone is now saying we need to activate our right brain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你看看《哈佛商业评论》以及人们在领导力方面讨论的话题，每个人现在都在说我们需要激活右脑。

sentences.en: Gallup just did a thing on this.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普刚就此做过一项调查。

sentences.en: Everyone is talking about this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在讨论这个。

sentences.en: We need to activate our right brains because we want to operate with a full brain.
sentences.zh: 我们需要激活右脑，因为我们希望用全脑来运作。

sentences.en: So when someone comes to you and says, what, you believe in all that stuff that I don't believe in?
sentences.zh: 所以，当有人来找你说，什么，你居然相信所有那些我不相信的东西？

sentences.en: Basically, you can just tell them I believe in a whole brain and it sounds like you only believe in using half of your brain.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你可以直接告诉他们，我相信的是全脑，听起来你只相信动用一半的大脑。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: That's the argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是论点。

sentences.en: It's not that one's right or one's wrong.
sentences.zh: 并不是说哪个对，哪个错。

sentences.en: It's how are you preferencing what you're looking at?
sentences.zh: 而是你如何去偏好你所看到的事物？

sentences.en: So, yes, certain things that you and I believe in, if you want to call it that, like the importance of dreams or imagination or fantasy or these kinds of things,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你和我所相信的某些东西，如果你想这么叫的话，比如梦想、想象力、幻想或这些类事物的重要性，

sentences.en: where creativity takes place, by the way, all of this is not measurable and it is just as real.
sentences.zh: 创造力诞生的地方，顺便说一句，所有这一切都是无法量化的，但它们同样真实。

sentences.en: I'll give you something in business that is not measurable, that is incredibly real.
sentences.zh: 我给你举一个商业中无法量化却又无比真实的事物。

sentences.en: It's called trust, right?
sentences.zh: 它叫信任，对吧？

sentences.en: TruSt.
sentences.zh: 信任。

sentences.en: Any business leader would say, oh, my God, I really have to truSt.
sentences.zh: 任何商界领袖都会说，天哪，我真的必须建立信任。

sentences.en: If people don't trust me, I'm not going to have a business.
sentences.zh: 如果人们不信任我，我就没法做生意。

sentences.en: I'm not going to have employees that stay and so on.
sentences.zh: 我也不会有愿意留下来的员工，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So trust isn't measurable, but it's very real.
sentences.zh: 所以信任是无法量化的，但它非常真实。

sentences.en: It's very tangible in that sense that it's real.
sentences.zh: 从这种真实性的意义上讲，它是非常具体的。

sentences.en: So that's a right brain capability.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种右脑能力。

sentences.en: So these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这些东西。

sentences.en: So all we're advocating for is to develop people's right brain capabilities.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们所倡导的全部内容，就是去发展人们的右脑能力。

sentences.en: I'm also very much in favor of left brain.
sentences.zh: 我也非常支持左脑。

sentences.en: I love left brain.
sentences.zh: 我热爱左脑。

sentences.en: I love that we have science and that we have an engineering degree, that we can have, you know, clean water and do good surgery.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我们拥有科学，拥有工程学位，能让我们拥有干净的水并实施出色的外科手术。

sentences.en: That's all wonderful, of course, but it's not enough.
sentences.zh: 这一切当然都很棒，但还不够。

sentences.en: It's only half of reality.
sentences.zh: 这只是现实的一半。

sentences.en: And in this complex world, we have to use our whole brain and we need to learn a language to do right brain development.
sentences.zh: 在这个复杂的世界里，我们必须运用整个大脑，我们需要学习一门语言来开展右脑开发。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: That's exactly what Archetypes of Work does.
sentences.zh: 这正是“工作原型”（Archetypes of Work）所做的事情。

sentences.en: It is a language that develops people's right brains and gives them access to their creativity,
sentences.zh: 它是一门语言，能够开发人们的右脑，并通过理解那些指引我们度过一生的内在模式，

sentences.en: their imagination by understanding these inner patterns that are what guide us through life.
sentences.zh: 让他们能够触及自己的创造力和想象力。

sentences.en: It's interesting, the quote about trees that you mentioned, I think, and you obviously know your father better than I do.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，你提到的关于树木的那段引言，我想，而且你显然比我更了解你的父亲。

sentences.en: And some of them were James Hillman, your dad's and the quote,

sentences.zh: 我觉得有时他在思考树木时甚至都没有明说，因为他懂得很多语言，掌握了很多哲学和认识论的方法，他把这些看作是分支出来的。

sentences.zh: 我正在为此听治疗CD，我不明白这和患者有什么关系之类的话。

sentences.en: And he was saying, like, you know, all of epistemology and philosophy, it branches off and it branches off.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，所有的认识论和哲学，它们不断分叉，不断分叉。

sentences.en: And, you know, a ton of the reason why we experience these things is just to say, well, I like Spinoza.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们体验到这些事情的很大一部分原因，只是为了说，嗯，我喜欢斯宾诺莎。

sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴你找到了你的思维方式，或者诸如此类的话。

sentences.zh: 他们只是在另一棵树上。

sentences.zh: 不过，认识到我们思维的后果是很重要的。

sentences.zh: 所以，如果我的思维方式认为所有右脑主导的事物都是错的，那么我就是在有意识且积极地排斥它。

sentences.en: I could also say I'm not comfortable with it.
sentences.zh: 我也可以说我对它感到不自在。

sentences.en: And I think you do see the people who hide in the metaphorical, mystical side of the brain, you know, probably around Jungian things.

sentences.zh: 我也挺赞同的。

sentences.zh: 总会觉得缺点什么。

sentences.en: It is a system that understands complexity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个理解复杂性的系统。

sentences.en: And this whole thing about having more than one voice inside, you know, developmental psychology typically says you're this, you know, first you crawl, then you walk, then you run.
sentences.zh: 而且关于内心有不止一个声音这回事，你知道的，发展心理学通常认为你是这样的，你知道的，先是爬，然后走，最后跑。

sentences.en: That's pretty much the model of most developmental psychologies.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是大多数发展心理学的模式。

sentences.en: And then behaviorism, you know, just comes in there.
sentences.zh: 然后行为主义，你知道的，就介入了。

sentences.en: And that's all about, you know, how are you behaving in a particular one of these phases.
sentences.zh: 这全都是关于，你知道的，你在其中某个特定阶段是如何表现的。

sentences.en: But all of these models have one thing in common.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些模式都有一个共同点。

sentences.en: They think of a human being as being singular inside.
sentences.zh: 它们都认为人类内部是单一的。

sentences.en: I am this.
sentences.zh: 我就是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, identity, the whole thing of identity, then you can get into identity politics and all these things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，身份认同，身份认同的整件事，然后你就会接触到身份政治和所有这些东西。

sentences.en: But these whole things that I am, that that's what gives me strength, my ego, is from an archetypal perspective, a bunch of baloney.
sentences.zh: 但这些关于“我是谁”的整套理论，也就是赋予我力量的东西，我的自我，从原型视角来看，全都是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Because there is no such thing as an I.
sentences.zh: 因为根本没有什么单一的“我”。

sentences.en: There are I's.
sentences.zh: 我们有许多个“我”。

sentences.en: There are multiple parts in us.
sentences.zh: 我们体内有多个部分。

sentences.en: And by the way, the way you can easily show this to someone who's a big believer in that interior I, that singular I.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你想向一个坚信内在只有一个“我”、一个单一“我”的人证明这一点，有个很简单的方法。

sentences.en: Have you ever had a conversation with yourself?
sentences.zh: 你跟自己对话过吗？

sentences.en: Well, of course I did this morning.
sentences.zh: 当然，我今天早上才刚说过。

sentences.en: I was wondering if I should have toast or cereal, you know.
sentences.zh: 我在纠结我是该吃吐司还是麦片，你知道的。

sentences.en: Or I was, and I should have this or should have that.
sentences.zh: 或者我在想，我该选这个还是选那个。

sentences.en: But of course, that's kind of a joke.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这听起来有点像个笑话。

sentences.en: But if you're like, should I stay with this person?
sentences.zh: 但如果你在想：我是该跟这个人在一起？

sentences.en: Should I leave this person?
sentences.zh: 还是离开这个人？

sentences.en: Should I keep this job?
sentences.zh: 我是该保留这份工作？

sentences.en: Or what about that?
sentences.zh: 或者那个怎么样？

sentences.en: I could take this job.
sentences.zh: 我可以接受这份工作。

sentences.en: But I have all these options.
sentences.zh: 但我有这么多选择。

sentences.en: Those conversations, weighing the pros and the cons, you can't do if you're a singular identity.
sentences.zh: 那些权衡利弊的对话，如果你是一个单一的身份，你是无法进行的。

sentences.en: You can only do that when you step away from yourself, whatever that self is.
sentences.zh: 只有当你从自己身上抽离出来时，无论那个“自己”是什么，你才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So to me, you're stepping from one inner character to another inner character.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，你是从一个内在角色切换到另一个内在角色。

sentences.en: And they're having a conversation.
sentences.zh: 它们正在进行对话。

sentences.en: And if you can identify who these characters are, that's very useful.
sentences.zh: 如果你能识别出这些都是些什么角色，那就太有用了。

sentences.en: Because then you know how they make decisions.
sentences.zh: 因为那样你就知道它们是如何做出决定的。

sentences.en: Is it the dreamer and the storyteller?
sentences.zh: 是梦想家和说书人吗？

sentences.en: Well, one's going to tell the other one a great story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个会给另一个讲一个精彩的故事。

sentences.en: And the other one's going to go into dreams and maybe not be so practical.
sentences.zh: 而另一个则会陷入梦想，可能就没那么务实了。

sentences.en: These are useful things to have as you recognize how we actually feel ourselves.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到我们实际上是如何感受自我时，这些都是很有用的认知。

sentences.en: We are peopled inside.
sentences.zh: 我们的内心居住了许多人。

sentences.en: You know, we are not singular inside.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的内心并非单一的。

sentences.en: That's what there's this lovely quote.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有一句很美的名言。

sentences.en: I have it in the beginning of one of my books.
sentences.zh: 我把它写在我其中一本书的开头。

sentences.en: This wonderful quote by Charles Simic.
sentences.zh: 这是查尔斯·西米奇的一句精彩名言。

sentences.en: He was the Poet Laureate in the United States a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 他几年前曾是美国的桂冠诗人。

sentences.en: He wrote, we do not live most of the time in exalted states.
sentences.zh: 他写道：我们绝大多数时间并不生活在狂喜的状态中。

sentences.en: The content of our stream of consciousness is usually not so lofty.
sentences.zh: 我们意识流的内容通常没有那么崇高。

sentences.en: Our psychic life is more like a squabbling theatrical company trying to rehearse a play we don't know the name of.
sentences.zh: 我们的心理生活更像是一个争吵不休的剧团，试图排练一出我们连名字都不知道的戏。

sentences.en: You know, that's really how it feels.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: There's this inner mess.
sentences.zh: 内心有一团乱麻。

sentences.en: Most of us can immediately relate to that.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都能立刻产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Now, when I wrote my dissertation, I found, you know, you always have to find the counterpoint, the counter voice.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我写博士论文时，我发现，你知道，你总是得寻找对立面，寻找反对的声音。

sentences.en: And I found a bunch of psychiatrists who are very, very afraid of this rule.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一群精神病学家，他们非常非常害怕这条规则。

sentences.en: Don't talk about multiplicity.
sentences.zh: 不要谈论多元性。

sentences.en: That's a completely different thing.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不同的另一回事。

sentences.en: That is an illness and has nothing to do with the way of speaking that we speak now.
sentences.zh: 那是一种疾病，与我们现在这种说话方式毫无关系。

sentences.zh: 把两者等同起来是极其天真和极其幼稚的。

sentences.zh: 多元性，内在多元性，是人类亿万年来对自己看法的一种方式。

sentences.en: If it was these, I mean, the gift of death psychology has been to bring us this inner multiplicity.

sentences.en: That's really been the greatest gift.
sentences.zh: 这真的是最伟大的贡献。

sentences.en: And then Jung gave them names and called them archetypes by looking at them globally.

sentences.en: But this is the big thing.
sentences.zh: 但这就是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: And now I just met a psychiatrist the other day who wrote an article and I connected with her because I've been writing about inner multiplicity in leadership.
sentences.zh: 然后我前几天刚遇到一位精神病学家，她写了一篇文章，我和她取得了联系，因为我一直在写关于领导力中的内在多元性的文章。

sentences.en: And she wrote one about, you know, from a psychiatrist's perspective, that maybe inner multiplicity doesn't mean dissociative identity disorder.
sentences.zh: 她写了一篇关于，从精神病学家的角度来看，内在多元性可能并不意味着分离性身份障碍。

sentences.en: It could really mean, you know, a richer way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可能意味着，你知道，一种更丰富的思考方式。

sentences.en: So I'm very interested in this sort of movement that's starting now.
sentences.zh: 所以我对现在兴起的这种运动非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And, well, it's been going on for a while, but now it's getting some traction that inner multiplicity is good.
sentences.zh: 而且，好吧，它已经持续了一段时间，但现在它开始获得一些关注，即内在多元性是件好事。

sentences.en: There is a language for it.
sentences.zh: 对此有一套专门的语言。

sentences.en: In our case, we use archetypes based on the planets.
sentences.zh: 在我们的案例中，我们使用的是基于行星的原型。

sentences.en: To me, that's a very solid foundation, 5,000 years of data.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个非常坚实的基础，拥有5000年的数据。

sentences.en: If you want to use left brain just to quantify that, of how, what the planets mean, you know, for a person.
sentences.zh: 如果你想用左脑来量化这一点，看看这些行星对一个人意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so, and so, you know, it's a tool.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，你知道，这是一种工具。

sentences.en: And when you say that, you mean that there's, you know, perennial patterns that we can go back and look at these things popping up.
sentences.zh: 当你这么说的时候，你的意思是，你知道，有一些历久弥新的模式，我们可以回过头去看看这些反复出现的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, because, I mean, that's my argument when people say, well, it's not empirical to look at mythology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为，这就是我的论点，当人们说，看神学是不经验主义的。

sentences.en: It's not empirical for you to look at these gurus and mystics that you're writing about on your blog.
sentences.zh: 你看你在博客上写的那些古鲁和神秘主义者，那不是经验主义的。

sentences.en: You know, why are you writing about Martin Buber?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你为什么要写马丁·布伯？

sentences.en: Why are you writing about Meister Eckhart?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要写埃克哈特大师？

sentences.en: And I'm saying, like, because when somebody invents Buddhism in the middle of medieval Germany, that means that there is some part of the brain that produces this.
sentences.zh: 而我说，就像是，当中世纪日德兰半岛中部有人发明了佛教时，这意味着大脑中产生这种东西的某个部分是存在的。

sentences.en: Because Meister Eckhart didn't go study in Japan, or he didn't go study, you know, in Thailand.
sentences.zh: 因为埃克哈特大师并没有去日本学习，他也没有去，你知道的，泰国学习。

sentences.en: And so, that means that this is a description.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着这是一种描述。

sentences.en: You know, people are universally arriving at these places because of archetypal or some kind of inborn thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们由于原型或某种天生的东西，普遍得出了这些结论。

sentences.en: And I don't care where you think it comes from.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎你认为它来自哪里。

sentences.en: You can have a woo-woo spiritual metaphysics.
sentences.zh: 你可以持有某种玄乎的精神形而上学。

sentences.en: You can have a scientific, genetically deterministic, biological deterministic metaphysics.
sentences.zh: 你可以持有科学的、基因决定论的、生物决定论的形而上学。

sentences.en: I'm just pointing out the pattern, you know.
sentences.zh: 我只是在指出这种模式，你知道的。

sentences.en: And if you can't see the pattern, that seems more empirical to me than people want it to be.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到这种模式，在我看来，这比人们想要的还要经验主义。

sentences.en: But isn't that a strange question to ask you?
sentences.zh: 但问你这样一个奇怪的问题难道不奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Why would you study Eckhart, or why would you study?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要研究埃克哈特，或者你为什么要研究？

sentences.en: In other words, to me, you know, you're a psychologist, you know.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，在我看来，你知道，你是个心理学家，你知道的。

sentences.zh: 今年夏天我和家人在西班牙，我们去了多尔曼·多明加，这是一处新石器时代的石棚墓。

sentences.en: And you're looking at this thing that is just unbelievably old that somebody moved 100 and 180 ton rocks to make this long tunnel so that we're exactly at the winter economics.
sentences.zh: 当你看着这个不可思议般古老的东西时，有人搬运了110吨和180吨重的岩石来建造这个长长的隧道，好让阳光在冬至时分，

sentences.en: The light would shine all the way down to the very tip of this tomb and touch the bones, you know, that were in the end.
sentences.zh: 能够一直照进这个墓穴的最深处，并照亮，你知道的，位于尽头的那些骨头。

sentences.en: And, you know, just it's one of the first things that we did.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这正是我们所做的最早的事情之一。

sentences.en: You know, you could look at somebody who, you know, there's a mountain, there's a storm.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以看到某个人，你知道，那里有一座山，有一场风暴。

sentences.en: I can build a house, but it'll burn down.
sentences.zh: 我可以盖一所房子，但它会被烧毁。

sentences.en: I can tell a story, but it'll change.
sentences.zh: 我可以讲一个故事，但它会变样。

sentences.en: And then you see you that birth of architecture where you build this thing.
sentences.zh: 然后你看到了建筑的诞生，你建造了这样宏伟的建筑。

sentences.en: The psyche is completely different because using math, using intuition, using logic, I'm now talking to God.
sentences.zh: 心灵的状态完全不同了，因为运用数学、运用直觉、运用逻辑，我此时正在与神对话。

sentences.en: You know, this 180 ton monument is going to be here forever, you know, from my mind.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在我的心目中，这座重达180吨的纪念碑将永远矗立在这里。

sentences.en: And it's connecting me to this timeless order of cosmology.
sentences.zh: 它将我与宇宙那永恒的秩序连接在一起。

sentences.en: I was able to predict the sun, you know, that moment of change.
sentences.zh: 我能够预测太阳，你知道的，那一刻的转变。

sentences.en: You know, that's like one of the moments we came alive in it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那就像是我们真正变得生机勃勃的时刻之一。

sentences.en: And it had to do with the cosmos, with the astro.
sentences.zh: 这与宇宙有关，与星象有关。

sentences.en: Very beautiful.
sentences.zh: 非常美妙。

sentences.en: And, you know, Joel, I think every religion started out, well, religion in general, started out as sun worshipping because, you know, the sun was the giver of life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，乔尔，我认为每一种宗教最初——好吧，总体上的宗教——最初都是从崇拜太阳开始的，因为，你知道，太阳是生命的给予者。

sentences.en: It's pretty natural to then make sun, you know, ra or in the Inca tradition.
sentences.zh: 因此，把太阳奉为神明是很自然的，你知道，比如拉神，或者印加传统中的太阳神。

sentences.en: You know, these were, you know, if you were sitting in your cave shivering and the sun didn't come up the next morning, you know, you'd be dead.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都是，如果你坐在山洞里瑟瑟发抖，而第二天太阳没有升起，你知道，你就会死掉。

sentences.en: No food, no light, no nothing.
sentences.zh: 没有食物，没有光亮，什么都没有。

sentences.en: So this idea that you would worship and ask the sun to come back every day makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这种顶礼膜拜并祈求太阳每天都回来的想法是非常合乎情理的。

sentences.en: So religion started out as sun and then sun gods and so on.
sentences.zh: 因此，宗教最初始于太阳，然后是太阳神，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the honoring of the sun and the moon and many traditions are based on the moon.
sentences.zh: 对太阳的崇敬以及许多基于月亮的传统。

sentences.en: And they're regular, they're predictable.
sentences.zh: 它们是有规律的，是可预测的。

sentences.en: We know where they are at any given time.
sentences.zh: 在任何给定的时间，我们都知道它们在哪里。

sentences.en: And so we set our calendars according to them, too, in a very, you know, sketchy world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也根据它们来设定我们的日历，在一个你知道的充满不确定性的世界里，

sentences.en: That is always reliable.
sentences.zh: 那是永远可靠的。

sentences.en: We know where the sun is going to be at any given time.
sentences.zh: 我们知道太阳在任何给定时间会在哪里。

sentences.en: We know where the moon is going to be at any given time so we can organize our chaotic lives according to them, which is why every calendar is made that way.
sentences.zh: 我们知道月亮在任何给定时间会在哪里，所以我们可以根据它们来安排我们混乱的生活，这就是为什么每个日历都是这样制作的。

sentences.en: Could you let people have some examples of how the archetypes at work could help them directly with leadership?
sentences.zh: 你能否向大家举几个例子，说明发挥作用的原型如何能直接帮助他们提升领导力？

sentences.en: If they're doing executive coaching, if they're doing mentoring, if they are a business leader, therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 如果他们从事高管教练、导师工作，如果他们是商业领袖、治疗师。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll give you a corporate example and I'll give you a personal example.
sentences.zh: 好的，我给你们举一个企业例子，再举一个个人例子。

sentences.en: First, the corporate example, a executive, an R&D department, research and development department had about 30 people in it.
sentences.zh: 首先是企业例子，一个高管，一个研发部门，即研究与开发部门，里面大约有30个人。

sentences.en: And the leadership looked at the numbers and they found that they'd been giving this department millions of dollars over the last five years and nothing really came out of this department that was useful.
sentences.zh: 领导层查看了数据，发现过去五年里他们一直在给这个部门投入数百万美元，但这个部门并没有产出什么真正有用的东西。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the first thought, what should we keep them?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，第一个想法是，我们应该留住他们吗？

sentences.en: Should we fire them?
sentences.zh: 我们应该解雇他们吗？

sentences.en: What should we do?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: Do we have the wrong people?
sentences.zh: 是我们招错人了吗？

sentences.en: Why, you know, this isn't working?
sentences.zh: 为什么，你知道，这行不通？

sentences.en: They should be inventing stuff and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他们本该搞发明创造之类的。

sentences.en: So, or improving stuff or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者改进产品之类的。

sentences.en: So they called us in.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们把我们请了去。

sentences.en: We did an assessment on everybody.
sentences.zh: 我们对每个人都进行了评估。

sentences.en: We have an archetypal assessment and found out that nobody in the team, not a single one of them, including the person who led the team, was comfortable with their inner renegade.
sentences.zh: 我们有一套原型评估方法，结果发现团队中没有人，没有一个人——包括团队负责人——能够适应他们内心的“叛逆者”。

sentences.en: We ranked them by how comfortable I am.
sentences.zh: 我们根据他们的适应程度对他们进行了排名。

sentences.en: Am I really comfortable with this one?
sentences.zh: 我真的对这个角色感到适应吗？

sentences.en: Is it kind of center stage in my life?
sentences.zh: 它是我生活中的核心舞台吗？

sentences.en: I can easily step into it and show it to the world?
sentences.zh: 我能否轻松地融入其中并向世人展现？

sentences.en: Or is it kind of offstage taking a nap in the green room?
sentences.zh: 还是它像是在后台化妆室里打盹？

sentences.en: So none of them had the renegade in the top three.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当中没有人的“叛逆者”排在前三位。

sentences.en: So we gave them this report to leadership and they're like, well, I guess, you know, in the old days, what they would have done is let's fire these people.
sentences.zh: 于是我们将这份报告交给领导层，他们的反应是，好吧，我想，你知道，在过去，他们会做出的选择是解雇这些人。

sentences.en: We have the wrong people.
sentences.zh: 我们招错人了。

sentences.en: They're not renegade enough.
sentences.zh: 他们不够叛逆。

sentences.en: The renegade is that part of us, in all of us, that is the inventor, the creative, outside of the box thinker, doesn't mind the rules, goes out and does different things.
sentences.zh: “叛逆者”是我们每个人体内都有的那一部分，他是发明家、富有创造力的人、跳出框框思考的人，不在乎清规戒律，敢于走出去做不同的事情。

sentences.en: And so we said, actually, you don't have to fire these people because we know that everyone within them has an inner renegade.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说，实际上，你们不必解雇这些人，因为我们知道每个人内心深处都有一个内在的叛逆者。

sentences.en: It's just that for some reason they're not activating, they're not showing it, they're not, maybe they don't dare.
sentences.zh: 只是出于某种原因，他们没有激活它，没有展现它，没有，也许他们不敢。

sentences.en: Maybe they're afraid if they, you know, stick out too much, they'll get fired.
sentences.zh: 也许他们害怕如果自己，你知道，表现得太出格，就会被解雇。

sentences.en: Maybe they were told as a kid, don't ever, you know, break the rules.
sentences.zh: 也许他们小时候被告知，千万不要，你知道，打破规则。

sentences.en: Doesn't matter why.
sentences.zh: 原因是什么并不重要。

sentences.en: We don't care why.
sentences.zh: 我们不在乎原因。

sentences.en: We just know that right now, nobody's showing up with a renegade center stage or sort of comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我们只知道现在没有人把叛逆者摆在中心舞台上，或者说他们对此感到很不自在。

sentences.en: So instead, we go in and we do a renegade activation workshop with that team.
sentences.zh: 因此，相反，我们介入并与该团队开展了一场“叛逆者激活”工作坊。

sentences.en: We did that over about two days.
sentences.zh: 我们大约花了两天时间完成了这项工作。

sentences.en: They loved it.
sentences.zh: 他们非常喜欢。

sentences.en: It was a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 过程非常有趣。

sentences.en: And within about six months, that team invented something rather well known.
sentences.zh: 大约在大约六个月内，那个团队发明了一个相当知名的东西。

sentences.en: So, you know, they broke out of their own limitations.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们突破了自身的局限。

sentences.en: And, of course,
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，

sentences.en: leadership was delighted because it costs them way less to activate an archetype than it does to fire everyone and hire new people and then start all over again with a new team.
sentences.zh: 领导层非常高兴，因为激活一个原型的成本，比解雇所有人、雇用新人然后用新团队重新开始要低得多。

sentences.en: So that's a practical example of how activating an archetype in a team,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个实际的例子，说明如何在团队中激活一个原型，

sentences.en: because you can do a team assessment as well and find out what is this team not so strong on and what is this team really strong on and that they might overplay and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为你也可以对团队进行评估，找出这个团队在哪些方面不太擅长，在哪些方面非常擅长，以及他们可能会过度使用哪些方面，等等。

sentences.en: So a personal example is someone who, you know, is a woman who wanted to activate her warrior more because it was at the bottom of her comfort liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以一个个人的例子是，你知道，有一个女性想要更多地激活她的“战士”原型，因为它处于她舒适区的底端。

sentences.en: You know, she wasn't comfortable with it for a lot of historical reasons, which in coaching you get into deeper things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，由于很多历史原因，她对它感到不自在，在教练辅导中你会深入探讨这些事情。

sentences.en: You know why someone might not like that in a business setting you usually don't.
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么在商业环境中，通常不会有人去探讨一个人为什么可能不喜欢那个原型。

sentences.en: But in this coaching with this woman, you know, there were a lot of reasons in her childhood and in her past that, you know, coming from a war-torn country and so on,
sentences.zh: 但在对这位女性的辅导中，你知道，她的童年和过去有很多原因，你知道，来自一个饱受战争蹂躏的国家等等，

sentences.en: where the warrior was not seen as anything she really wanted to access.
sentences.zh: 在那里，“战士”并不被视为她真正想要接触的任何东西。

sentences.en: Very well understood.
sentences.zh: 这完全可以理解。

sentences.en: But she also saw the cost of not accessing that part of herself.
sentences.zh: 但她也看到了不去接触自己那一部分所付出的代价。

sentences.en: And so we did a whole bunch of work.
sentences.zh: 于是我们做了大量的工作。

sentences.en: And that means, you know, giving her homework every week and doing certain things and writing things and reflecting on this, that, and the other.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，你知道，每周给她布置家庭作业，做一些特定的事情，写东西，反思这个、那个以及其他事情。

sentences.en: And it completely changed her marriage, for one thing.
sentences.zh: 首先，这彻底改变了她的婚姻。

sentences.en: She was just about ready to leave her husband when that started.
sentences.zh: 刚开始时，她几乎准备离开她的丈夫了。

sentences.en: And then, you know, now it's all, you know, going really, really great and they're communicating.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，现在一切，你知道，都进展得非常非常顺利，他们开始沟通了。

sentences.en: It's a whole new thing.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个全新的局面。

sentences.en: That would never have happened had she not found that inner power to speak up for what she needed and so forth.
sentences.zh: 如果她没有找到那种内在的力量去说出自己的需求等等，这一切就永远不会发生。

sentences.en: So it's a lovely thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件美好的事。

sentences.en: And she had externalized a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 而且她把很多东西都外化了。

sentences.en: Her husband is very warrior sort of type and classic sort of that sort of, you know, goes out and gets what he needs and does and is good at business and these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫非常具有“战士”那种类型，属于经典的、你知道的会出去争取自己所需、付诸行动、精通商业的那种人。

sentences.en: So she's learning that she doesn't have to give that away.
sentences.zh: 所以她正在学习，她不必把这部分能力拱手让人。

sentences.en: She can actually own it and have an honest and serious and good conversation with her husband in one place.
sentences.zh: 她实际上可以拥有它，并在同一个平台上与丈夫进行诚恳、严肃且良好的对话。

sentences.en: But also her other life with her kids and with her and with her work and everything else also changed dramatically over the last about six months of coaching.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，她在照顾孩子、生活、工作以及其他各方面的生活，在过去大约六个月的教练辅导中也发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: So, you know, this is a practical example of how activating an archetype can help you.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个实际的例子，说明激活原型如何能够帮助你。

sentences.en: It helped her in her career.
sentences.zh: 它在她的职业生涯中帮到了她。

sentences.en: She has a business.
sentences.zh: 她拥有自己的业务。

sentences.en: It got much better there.
sentences.zh: 那里的情况变得好多了。

sentences.en: People weren't walking all over her because, you know, had, you know, her own power back and things like that.
sentences.zh: 人们不再骑在她头上，因为，你知道，她找回了属于自己的力量，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So there are no good or bad archetypes.
sentences.zh: 所以原型没有好坏之分。

sentences.en: It's just how comfortable are you with them and are you able to express them in a productive way or not?
sentences.zh: 关键在于你对它们的熟悉程度如何，以及你是否能够以富有成效的方式表达它们？

sentences.en: So that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: So the way people can get to know more about archetypes at work is to go to archetypes at work.com.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们了解更多职场原型的途径是访问 archetypes at work.com。

sentences.en: And then they can connect with me directly and tell me what their needs are.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可以直接与我联系，告诉我他们的需求是什么。

sentences.en: Is it personal coaching?
sentences.zh: 是个人教练辅导吗？

sentences.en: Is it a corporate thing?
sentences.zh: 是企业项目吗？

sentences.en: Is it a leadership team?
sentences.zh: 是领导力团队吗？

sentences.en: Is it a board that's not functioning ideally?
sentences.zh: 是一个运作不够理想的董事会吗？

sentences.en: Is it, you know, an intact team?
sentences.zh: 是一个，你知道的，现有的完整团队吗？

sentences.en: Is it just a bunch of people who are not an intact team, but they're all in the same organization?
sentences.zh: 还是只是一群并非完整团队、但都在同一组织中的人？

sentences.en: There's so many ways to approach this.
sentences.zh: 有很多方法可以切入这一点。

sentences.en: All archetypes at work work starts with a problem.
sentences.zh: 所有职场原型的工作都始于一个问题。

sentences.en: What's your problem?
sentences.zh: 你的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Like in this case, you know, R&D department isn't inventing anything.
sentences.zh: 比如在这个例子中，你知道，研发部门什么也没发明出来。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是个问题。

sentences.en: You know, we have high turnover.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的人员流动率很高。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是个问题。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to work here.
sentences.zh: 没有人想在这里工作。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是个问题。

sentences.en: We can't find more people.
sentences.zh: 我们找不到更多的人。

sentences.en: That's a problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是个问题。

sentences.en: In other words, we're not attractive.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们缺乏吸引力。

sentences.en: Our lover isn't really at the forefront.
sentences.zh: 我们的“情人”原型并没有真正处于前沿。

sentences.en: People aren't wanting to work with us.
sentences.zh: 人们不想和我们合作。

sentences.en: These kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So we then translate the problem into an archetypal pattern and then think about ways to solve it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将问题转化为原型模式，然后思考解决问题的方法。

sentences.en: And what would that mean with different options?
sentences.zh: 面对不同的选择，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: And there's a team of people who are trained.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个受过培训的团队。

sentences.en: We have a guild of practitioners.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个从业者公会。

sentences.en: These are people who are trained by us who can go out and do the work and are licensed to do it and know it very well.
sentences.zh: 这些人接受过我们的培训，可以开展相关工作，获得了执业资格并且对此非常熟悉。

sentences.en: They've done a lot of training to get, you know, capable to do the work well.
sentences.zh: 他们接受了大量的培训，以便，你知道的，有能力把工作做好。

sentences.en: And so they can find someone, you know, on that page as well and who can help them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也可以在这个网页上找到某个人，来帮助他们。

sentences.en: I think we're speaking 11 languages amongst us now, the guild members.
sentences.zh: 我想我们公会成员内部现在说11种语言。

sentences.en: And so it's quite global and it's quite, I've translated the work into about 16 languages at this point, including that just got Swahili,
sentences.zh: 所以它的全球化程度很高，而且，我目前已经将这项工作翻译成了大约16种语言，包括刚刚加入的斯瓦希里语，

sentences.en: which is kind of cool because it's the most spoken language in Africa.
sentences.zh: 这挺酷的，因为它是非洲使用人数最多的语言。

sentences.en: So this is a language that is easily understood because archetypes are universal.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种很容易被理解的语言，因为原型是普世的。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if we're working with yam farmers in Africa, which we have, or with, you know, engineers in India or with, you know,
sentences.zh: 无论我们是在和非洲的山药种植者合作（我们确实合作过），还是和，你知道的，印度的工程师合作，或者和，你知道的，

sentences.en: a small team of professionals in the United States.
